_comment: Static shaper metadata overlay. Keys are engine-reported names (join by name at runtime; engine enumerations are the sole authority for names/IDs/order — architecture §2). Prose from HQPlayer Desktop 6.0.0 manual §4.4 (dither) / §4.5 (modulator); rate thresholds from manual statements. All rate constraints are manufacturer recommendations ('optimized for', 'recommended'). The UI grays sdm_modulators below their floor with reason text and never hides them; pcm_dithers gray nowhere, since a dither below its floor still produces output. Either family below its floor also raises an alert-strip row — crit for modulators, warn for dithers (architecture §5). `needs_external_volume` marks a modulator whose limited SNR assumes the volume control sits outside HQPlayer: staging it while HQPlayer's own volume control is live asks the user to confirm first, and so does un-pinning the volume while one is already selected (store/guards.js). Apply asks again over the whole staged configuration, for the routes that assemble one without a per-field edit (preset preview, the wire-name staging lane).
_join_note: Match engine name to key case-sensitively. If no exact match, normalize both sides (casefold, collapse spaces) before declaring a gap.

guidance.order: Fifth order modulators are more suitable for DACs that have simple analog reconstruction filters. Seventh order modulators provide better technical performance, but also put more demands on the DAC's analog reconstruction filter. Typically this means that fifth order modulators suit DACs that have one switching element while seventh order modulators have potential for better performance on DACs that have multi-element switching arrays. For ESS Sabre based DACs, fifth order modulators are recommended. For most other DACs, seventh order modulators are optimal.
guidance.type: DSD* modulators are fixed configuration ones while ASDM* modulators are adaptive in various ways based on source signal.

AHM5EC5L.description: Experimental fifth order five level hybrid modulator with extended compensation. Optimized for rates ≥ 40.96 MHz.
AHM5EC5L.notes: Limited SNR compared to other modulators, best suited for a loudspeaker system and/or when digital volume control is not needed. Not recommended when HQPlayer's volume control is the primary volume control method.

AHM7EC5L.description: Experimental seventh order five level hybrid modulator with extended compensation. Optimized for rates ≥ 40.96 MHz.

AHM5EC8B.description: Fifth order 8-bit hybrid modulator with extended compensation. Optimized for rates ≥ 40.96 MHz. Bandwidth optimized to provide enough flat noise floor bandwidth for practically all hi-res content.

AHM7EC8B.description: Seventh order 8-bit hybrid modulator with extended compensation. Optimized for rates ≥ 40.96 MHz. Bandwidth optimized to provide enough flat noise floor bandwidth for practically all hi-res content.

none.description: No noise-shaping or dithering, only rounding. Mostly suitable for testing cases together with none filter selection, where bit-perfect output is needed. Not recommended.

NS1.description: Simple first order noise-shaping. Sample values are rounded and the quantization error is shaped in such a way that the error energy is pushed to the higher frequencies. Suitable mostly for 176.4/192 kHz upsampling.
NS1.notes: Use of "NS1" with equipment sensitive to ultrasonic noise is not recommended.

NS4.description: Fourth order noise-shaping. Similar in shape to the "shaped" dither. Suitable for all rates ≥ 88.2 kHz.

NS5.description: Fifth order noise-shaping. Fairly aggressive noise-shaping designed for 8x and 16x rates (352.8/384/705.6/768 kHz). Not recommended for rates below 192 kHz.
NS5.notes: Especially good for PCM1704 at those highest rates.

NS9.description: Ninth order noise-shaping. Very aggressive noise-shaping designed especially for 4x rates (176.4/192 kHz) and recommended for these rates.
NS9.notes: Especially good for older 16-bit, 4x-rate-capable multibit DACs like TDA154x etc.

LNS15.description: 15th order linear noise-shaping. Smooth noise-shaping slope designed especially for 16x rates (705.6/768 kHz) and recommended for these higher PCM rates. Can be also used at 8x rates (352.8/384 kHz), but not recommended for rates below.

RPDF.description: Rectangular Probability Density Function. White noise dither. Computationally lightweight, but only suitable for 24-bit or higher output hardware.

TPDF.description: Triangular Probability Density Function. This is the industry standard simple dither mechanism. Suitable for any rate and recommended if the playback rate is 44.1/48 kHz. Recommended for general purpose use.

Gauss1.description: Gaussian Probability Density Function. High quality flat frequency dither recommended for rates ≤ 96 kHz where noise-shaping is not suitable.

shaped.description: Shaped dither. Noise used in this dither has a shaped frequency distribution to lower the audibility of the dither noise. Suitable for playback rates ≥ 88.2/96 kHz.
